verdict.rationale: Wally's CLI runs both local models (offline, no account) and RunAnywhere's own hosted Wally Cloud models through the same tools. An explicit `--cloud` flag switches between hosted and local execution. However, the only cloud backend evidenced is RunAnywhere's first-party hardware, not third-party cloud AI providers. Missing for 10: connecting third-party cloud providers (e.g., OpenAI or Anthropic keys) alongside local models, a single unified interface spanning multiple providers, and independent hands-on corroboration of the local/cloud switching.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can connect to cloud AI providers alongside local models within the same interface

citations.quote: Cloud models run on RunAnywhere's hardware instead of the user's, so you can use models too large for a laptop while keeping the same tools.
When a small model on your own machine is enough, the same CLI runs it, offline and without an account.
`--cloud` is an `opencode` flag: it asks for the hosted model rather than one on this machine.
Hosted and local execution are explicit choices.
